neighbours.label: The English token 'late'/'Late' itself, in any sense (late grandfather, late show, late 1800s, Late fees, running late), strongest as a modifier before a noun or time phrase; not later/latest, not words containing 'late' (translate, chocolate), not lateness without the word (delayed, tardy)
fire: My late grandfather built this house by hand.
The late show starts right after the news.
Late fees apply if you return the book after Friday.
In the late eighteenth century, the canal was dug.
We stayed up late talking about old friends.
Late on Tuesday, the senator announced her decision.
The bus was late again, so I walked to work.
The late afternoon light filled the kitchen.
quiet: My dear grandfather built this house by hand.
The night show starts right after the news.
Extra fees apply if you return the book after Friday.
In the early eighteenth century, the canal was dug.
We stayed up talking about old friends until dawn.
Later on Tuesday, the senator announced her decision.
The bus was delayed again, so I walked to work.
The golden afternoon light filled the kitchen.
